en: Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Khalid ibn Abdillah informed us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever kills a gecko with the first blow, he will have such and such good deeds; whoever kills it with the second blow, he will have such and such good deeds, less than the first; and if he kills it with the third blow, he will have such and such good deeds, less than the second."

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah narrated to me—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from A'ishah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called the gecko: "the little noxious pest." Harmalah added: She said: "And I did not hear him order that it be killed."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—they said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Amir ibn Sa'd, from his father: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ordered the killing of geckos and called them "little noxious pests."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed me; (Second chain) and Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us: Rawh narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us; (Third chain) and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bakr informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Abd al-Hamid ibn Jubayr ibn Shaybah informed me that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed him that Umm Sharik informed him that she consulted the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about killing geckos, and he commanded that they be killed. And Umm Sharik was one of the women of Banu Amir ibn Lu'ayy. The wording of the hadith of Ibn Abi Khalaf and Abd ibn Humayd agreed, and the hadith of Ibn Wahb is close to it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Amr al-Naqid, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us—Ishaq said: informed us, and the others said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Jubayr ibn Shaybah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Umm Sharik: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ordered her to kill geckos. And in the hadith of Ibn Abi Shaybah: "he commanded" (without "her").

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ibn Ajlan: Sayfi narrated to me, from Abu al-Sa'ib, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: I heard him say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, in Medina there is a group of jinn who have accepted Islam. So whoever sees any of these dwellers, let him warn it three times; then if it appears to him after that, let him kill it, for it is a devil."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Wahb ibn Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us: my father narrated to us, saying: I heard Asma' ibn Ubayd narrating from a man named al-Sa'ib—and he is, according to us, Abu al-Sa'ib—who said: "We entered upon Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and while we were sitting, we heard movement beneath his bed. We looked, and behold, there was a snake..." and he cited the hadith with its story similar to the hadith of Malik from Sayfi, and said in it: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, these houses have dwellers; so if you see any of them, warn them three times. If it leaves, fine; otherwise kill it, for it is a disbeliever." And he said to them: "Go and bury your companion."

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Sarh narrated to me: Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Malik ibn Anas informed me, from Sayfi—and according to us he is the freed slave of Ibn Aflah: Abu al-Sa'ib, the freed slave of Hisham ibn Zuhrah, informed me that he entered upon Abu Sa'id al-Khudri in his home. He said: I found him praying, so I sat waiting for him until he finished his prayer. Then I heard a rustling among some dried date-palm branches in a corner of the house. I turned around and behold, there was a snake! I jumped up to kill it, but he gestured to me to sit down. So I sat down. When he finished the prayer, he pointed to a room in the house and said: "Do you see that room?" I said: "Yes." He said: "There was a young man among us who was newly married. We went out with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to the Trench, and that young man used to ask permission of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) at midday to return to his family. One day he asked his permission, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: 'Take your weapons with you, for I fear Banu Qurayzah may harm you.' The man took his weapons and returned, and behold, his wife was standing between the two doorposts. He lowered his spear toward her to pierce her with it, overcome by jealousy, but she said to him: 'Withhold your spear and enter the house to see what brought me outside!' He entered, and behold, there was a huge snake coiled upon the bed! He lunged at it with the spear and pierced it, then went out and planted the spear in the courtyard; the snake writhed upon it, and it is not known which of them died more quickly: the snake or the young man." He said: "So we came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), mentioned that to him, and said: 'Pray to Allah to bring him back to life for us!' He said: 'Ask forgiveness for your companion.' Then he said: 'Indeed, in Medina there are jinn who have accepted Islam. So if you see any of them, give it warning for three days; and if it appears to you after that, kill it, for it is only a devil.'"

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Hafs—meaning Ibn Ghiyath—narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from Abdullah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) commanded a person in ihram to kill a snake in Mina.

Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us: my father narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us: Ibrahim narrated to me, from al-Aswad, from Abdullah, who said: "While we were with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in a cave..." the like of the hadith of Jarir and Abu Mu'awiyah.
Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—they said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is that of Yahya; Yahya and Ishaq said: informed us, and the other two said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from Abdullah, who said: We were with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in a cave when "By the emissaries, sent forth one after another" was revealed to him. While we were taking it fresh from his mouth, a snake came out toward us. He said: "Kill it!" So we rushed to kill it, but it outpaced us. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Allah has saved it from your harm just as He saved you from its harm."

Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Usamah narrated to me that Nafi' narrated to him that Abu Lubabah passed by Ibn Umar while he was at the fortress near the house of Umar ibn al-Khattab watching for a snake, similar to the hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd.

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Jahdam informed us: Isma'il—and according to us he is Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from Umar ibn Nafi', from his father, who said: Abdullah ibn Umar was one day by some ruins belonging to him when he saw the glint of a small snake. He said: "Follow this small snake and kill it." Abu Lubabah al-Ansari said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbidding the killing of the harmless house snakes that inhabit homes, except for the short-tailed snake and the two-striped viper, for they are the two that blind the sight and cause miscarriages in pregnant women."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab—meaning al-Thaqafi—narrated to us, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Sa'id saying: Nafi' informed me that Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir al-Ansari—and he used to live in Quba' then moved to Medina—while Abdullah ibn Umar was sitting with him opening a small door of his, they came across a snake from the house-dwelling snakes and intended to kill it. Abu Lubabah said: "It has indeed been forbidden to kill them"—meaning the house-dwelling snakes—"and it was commanded to kill the short-tailed snake and the two-striped viper, and it was said: 'They are the two that snatch away the eyesight and cause pregnant women to miscarry.'"

Ishaq ibn Musa al-Ansari narrated it to us: Anas ibn Iyad narrated to us: Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Abdullah ibn Umar, from Abu Lubabah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); (Second chain) and Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma' al-Duba'i narrated to me: Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Abdullah: that Abu Lubabah informed him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade killing the snakes that live in houses.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Yahya—and he is al-Qattan—narrated to us, from Ubaydullah: Nafi' informed me that he heard Abu Lubabah informing Ibn Umar that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade killing house snakes.

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us: Nafi' narrated to us, who said: Ibn Umar used to kill all snakes until Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir al-Badri narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade killing house snakes, so he desisted.

Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to me: al-Layth informed us; (Second chain) and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us—and the wording is his: Layth narrated to us, from Nafi': that Abu Lubabah spoke to Ibn Umar asking him to open a door in his house to make it closer for him to go to the mosque. The young servants found the skin of a snake, so Abdullah said: "Look for it and kill it." Abu Lubabah said: "Do not kill it, for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade killing the snakes that are in houses."

Hajib ibn al-Walid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to us, from al-Zubaydi, from al-Zuhri: Salim ibn Abdillah informed me, from Ibn Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) commanding the killing of dogs, saying: "Kill snakes and dogs, and kill the two-striped viper and the short-tailed snake, for they snatch away eyesight and cause pregnant women to miscarry." Al-Zuhri said: "We consider that to be from their venom, and Allah knows best." Salim said: Abdullah ibn Umar said: "So I continued not leaving any snake that I saw without killing it. Then one day, while I was chasing a snake from among the house-dwelling snakes, Zayd ibn al-Khattab or Abu Lubabah passed by me while I was chasing it, and said: 'Gently, O Abdullah!' I said: 'The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ordered that they be killed.' He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) has forbidden killing house-dwelling snakes.'" And Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated it to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me; (Second chain) and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us; (Third chain) and Hasan al-Hulwani narrated to us: Ya'qub narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih; all of them from al-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission, except that Salih said: "until Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir and Zayd ibn al-Khattab saw me, and both of them said: 'He has forbidden killing house-dwelling snakes.'" And in the hadith of Yunus: "Kill snakes," and he did not say "the two-striped viper and the short-tailed snake."

Amr ibn Muhammad al-Naqid narrated to me: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "Kill snakes, and the two-striped viper and the short-tailed snake, for they cause pregnant women to miscarry and they snatch away eyesight." He said: So Ibn Umar used to kill every snake he found, until Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir or Zayd ibn al-Khattab saw him while he was chasing a snake, and said: "He has forbidden killing house-dwelling snakes."
Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us: Abu Mu'awiyah informed us: Hisham informed us, with this chain of transmission, and he said: "the short-tailed snake and the two-striped viper."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abdah ibn Sulayman and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Hisham; (Second chain) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abdah narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ordered the killing of the two-striped viper, for it snatches away eyesight and harms pregnancy.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hushaym informed us; (Second chain) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Sharik ibn Abdillah and Hushaym ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Ya'la ibn Ata', from Amr ibn al-Sharid, from his father, who said: There was a leper in the delegation of Thaqif, so the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sent word to him: "We have indeed accepted your pledge of allegiance, so you may return."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Anazi narrated to us: Yahya—meaning Ibn Sa'id—narrated to us, from Ubaydullah, from Nafi', from Safiyyah, from one of the wives of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Whoever goes to a fortune-teller and asks him about anything, his prayer will not be accepted for forty nights."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Abu Amr al-Awza'i narrated to us; (Second chain) and Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah narrated to us—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me; (Third chain) and Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me: al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us: Ma'qil—meaning Ibn Ubaydillah—narrated to us; all of them from al-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission, except that Yunus said: from Abdullah ibn Abbas: Some men from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah from the Ansar informed me... and in the hadith of al-Awza'i: "but they mix into it and add to it." And in the hadith of Yunus: "but they interpolate into it and add to it." And in the hadith of Yunus it was added: And Allah said: "Until when fear is removed from their hearts, they will say: 'What has your Lord said?' They will say: 'The truth.'" And in the hadith of Ma'qil it is as al-Awza'i said: "but they mix into it and add to it."

Hasan ibn Ali al-Hulwani and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—Hasan said: Ya'qub narrated to us, and Abd said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to me: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab: Ali ibn Husayn narrated to me that Abdullah ibn Abbas said: A man from the companions of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) from the Ansar informed me that while they were sitting one night with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), a shooting star shot across and flared with light. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to them: "What did you used to say during the Pre-Islamic Period of Ignorance when a shooting star like this was cast?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best. We used to say: 'A great man was born tonight, or a great man died.'" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "It is not shot on account of anyone's death or life. Rather, when our Lord—Blessed and Exalted is His Name—decrees a matter, the bearers of the Throne glorify Him, then the inhabitants of the heaven who are next to them glorify Him, until the glorification reaches the inhabitants of this lowest heaven. Then those who are next to the bearers of the Throne say to the bearers of the Throne: 'What did your Lord say?' And they inform them what He said." He said: "Then the inhabitants of the heavens inquire of one another until the news reaches this lowest heaven. Then the jinn snatch what they can overhear and cast it down to their allies, and missiles are shot at them. Whatever they convey accurately is the truth, but they mix falsehood into it and add to it."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Muhammad ibn Amr informed me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Shihab, with this chain of transmission, similar to the narration of Ma'qil from al-Zuhri.

Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me: al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us: Ma'qil—and he is Ibn Ubaydillah—narrated to us, from al-Zuhri: Yahya ibn Urwah informed me that he heard Urwah saying: A'ishah said: People asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about soothsayers, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to them: "They are nothing." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, sometimes they tell us something and it turns out to be true!" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "That is a word of truth which a jinni snatches and clucks into the ear of his ally like the clucking of a hen, and they mix more than a hundred lies into it."

Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Yahya ibn Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, from A'ishah, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, the soothsayers used to tell us something and we would find it to be true." He said: "That is a true word that the jinni snatches and casts into the ear of his ally, and adds to it a hundred lies."
